Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No. 486/16 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at PS. Prashant Vihar, with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 15.05.2016 at about 17:30 hrs, Near Bank of Baroda, Japanese Park, Rohini, Delhi, involving Car bearing registration no. DL8C-AL-9172 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4)
of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 09.05.2025 2.
According to DAR, on 15.05.2016, the petitioner was coming towards K.N.K. Marg from Rithala Metro Station side on motorcycle bearing no. DL8S-BT-0623.

At about 5:30 PM, when he reached Near Bank of Baroda, Japanese Park, Rohini, Delhi, one I-10 car bearing registration no.
DL8C-AL-9172 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from the side of Japanese Park and took a sharp U Turn and hit against the motorcycle of petitioner, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter, petitioner was taken to Max Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, where he was medically examined.
A case u/s. 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Prashant Vihar vide FIR No. 486/16 on the statement of petitioner.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with HDFC Ergo General Insurance Company Ltd /respondent no. 3 during the period in question.

8. The onus to prove the aforesaid issue was placed on the petitioner.
To prove the said issue, the injured examined himself as PW1 by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A).
In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), injured has deposed on the lines of averments made in the DAR petition.

He has relied upon the following documents:-

He further deposed that at about 5:30 Amit Verma vs Shreya Aggarwal on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132373827/
3 PM, when he reached Near Bank of Baroda, Japanese Park, Rohini, Delhi, offending vehicle i.e., I-10 car bearing registration no. DL8C-AL-9172 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner, came from the side of Japanese Park and took a U Turn and in that process, offending vehicle hit his motorcycle, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He further deposed that thereafter, MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS.

He further deposed that FIR was also lodged on his statement.
He categorically deposed that the accident took place due to sole rash, negligent and zigzag driving of offending vehicle by its driver.

10. During his cross-examination on behalf of driver and owner, he denied the suggestion that the accident in question occurred due to his own negligence as he was driving the motorcycle in zigzag manner.
He deposed that he was wearing helmet and slipper at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that accident did not occur due to the negligence of driver of alleged offending car.
He volunteered that as he had photograph of the registration number of the offending car as such he did not remember its number.
He denied the suggestion that IO of the case had taken the photographs of offending vehicle as well as its registration number not his relatives.
He denied the suggestion that he was driving his motorcycle at high speed due to which he could not control over his motorcycle and dashed the same against the divider.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company
, he deposed that the accident in question occurred on 15.05.2016 at about 5:45 pm in front of Bank of Baroda, Sector - 11, Rohini, Delhi when he was going to his home on his motorcycle.
He deposed that he could not say as from which direction, the offending car came and hit him.
He further deposed that the driver of the offending car stopped the vehicle after the accident and took him to the hospital.
He further deposed that he did not know as to who informed the police about the accident.
He deposed that MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 09.05.2025 police obtained his signatures on some blank papers.
He deposed that police did not ask him anything about the accident.
He further deposed that police did not take him to the spot of accident after the accident.
He further deposed that his relatives took the photograph of the registration number of the offending car after the accident.
He admitted that his relatives told him the registration number of the offending car.
He further admitted that none of his relative was present at the spot at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that some another vehicle had hit him on the date of accident.

11. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination despite he being cross-examined at length by the respondents and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
Moreover, FIR No. 486/2016(which is part of DAR) is shown to have been registered on the statement of petitioner himself on the date of accident itself i.e., 15.05.2016.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant/petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
On the other hand, none of the respondents examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 during the course of inquiry.

Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No.

12. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the criminal case, have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely Ms. Shreya Aggarwal has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s. 279/338 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

13. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

18 . The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Hon'ble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
19.

These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
"10. The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

11. The general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 09.05.2025 would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".

Petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that he was Manufacturer and Retailer of gold, silver and diamond jewellery and was earning Rs. 30,000/- per month.
For this, he has relied upon copy of his ITR(which is part of DAR) for the Assessment Year 2015-16.
A perusal of said ITR shows that the same was filed on 20.06.2016 and the date of accident in the present case is 15.05.2016 and thus, the said ITR was filed after the accident.
Therefore, the said ITR can not be considered for computation of loss of income of petitioner.
However, the petitioner has filed copy of Migration Certificate in the DAR which shows that he had passed Secondary School Examination from National Institute of Open Schooling in April 2008.
Hence, the monthly income of injured is being assessed as per applicable minimum wages of a Matriculate person, as on the date of accident i.e. 15.05.2016.
The minimum wages of a Matriculate person were Rs. 11,622/- per month.
MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 09.05.2025 26
. The treatment record i.e., Discharge Summary of Max Hospital (which is also part of DAR), of petitioner shows that he had suffered crush injury right leg with nerovascular damage right leg.
As per said discharge summary, petitioner was admitted in the aforesaid hospital on 15.05.2016 and was discharged on 18.05.2016.
Further, he filed certain medical bills and treatment record.

In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess work in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained crush injury right leg with nerovascular damage right leg as mentioned in his treatment record due to the accident.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and continuous treatment record filed on record, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at least for a period of 6 months or so including his recovery period.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 69,732/- (Rs. 11,622/- x 6) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 60% in relation to his right lower limb and there was amputation of right lower limb (below knee).

Keeping in view the nature of injuries MACP No. 7003/16; FIR No. 486/16.; PS. Prashant Vihar DOD: 09.05.2025 suffered by the petitioner, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/-

LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 29.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 60% in relation to his right lower limb and there was amputation of right lower limb (below knee).
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him and his continued treatment for considerable period and the permanent disability suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.

33. Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case including the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner as well as the disability suffered by him, his functional disability is taken as 30% with regard to whole body.
34. In copy of Aadhaar Card of petitioner, his date of birth is mentioned as 10.11.1992.
